faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate as a secondary school teacher in Victoria?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $40 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040 gross per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates. Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual estimate.

faqs.q: Does the 25% casual loading apply to a secondary school teacher salary in Victoria?
faqs.a: Casual loading of 25% is added on top of the base hourly rate for casual employees under many awards. If you are a casual secondary school teacher, your employer may pay a higher rate that already includes the loading. When using [the timesheet](/), tick the '25% casual loading' checkbox only if your base rate does not already include it. The calculator then adds the loading to show your total hourly rate.

faqs.q: What tax and super should I expect on a secondary school teacher salary in Victoria?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top by your employer, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. These are estimates; see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Secondary School Teacher Salary Victoria

If you are a secondary school teacher in Victoria or considering the role, you likely want to know how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay. This guide explains the conversion formula, the different pay structures under Australian workplace laws, and how to use [the timesheet](/) to get a quick estimate. Remember, the figures here are estimates based on standard assumptions; your actual pay may vary due to awards, enterprise agreements, or individual contracts.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual

The basic formula to calculate annual gross pay from an hourly rate is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours (as defined by the Fair Work Act). So if your hourly rate is $45, your annual gross would be $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above, weekly pay is $45 × 38 = $1,710, so fortnightly gross is $3,420. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## Different Pay Rates: Minimum Wage, Awards, and Casual Loading

Australia has a multi-tiered wage system. It is important to know which rate applies to you.

### National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This is the legal floor; most secondary school teachers are covered by awards or agreements that pay more.

### Award Rates and Enterprise Agreements

Secondary school teachers in Victoria are typically covered by the *Teachers (Victorian Government Schools) Agreement* or similar state awards. These set minimum salaries based on classification and experience. The rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a graduate teacher might earn around $75,000 per year, while an experienced leading teacher can earn over $120,000. These are not medians but examples; actual pay depends on your specific role and agreement.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual secondary school teacher, your hourly rate should include a 25% casual loading on top of the base award rate. When using [the timesheet](/), do **not** enter a rate that already includes the loading. Instead, enter the base rate and tick the '25% casual loading' checkbox. The calculator will add the loading automatically.

## Example: Average Earnings in Victoria

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria are $2,041.10 per week. This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for secondary school teachers. It gives a general benchmark. Using the formula, that weekly figure corresponds to an annual gross of about $106,137 (assuming 52 weeks). However, your actual secondary school teacher salary in Victoria may differ.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $90,000, your employer contributes an additional $10,800 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your taxable income and the tax rates for 2026–27. The resident tax scale is:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). No HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging is deducted in this estimate. Use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a more detailed calculator.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [the timesheet](/) is the home page of our site. You enter your base hourly rate, select whether you are casual (to add the 25% loading), and the tool instantly shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. It is designed for all Australian workers, including secondary school teachers in Victoria.

## Important Notes

- This guide assumes a 38-hour week. If you work different hours, adjust the formula accordingly.
- Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed pay guides, visit [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data). You can also check [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for state and national averages, and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for other occupations.
